headline: City services rank high in Ward 20 while every measure of money sits at the bottom.
summary:
The split in this ward's numbers is the story. Garbage carts get serviced sixth-fastest in the city, permit-parking pressure is among the lowest, nearly all of the ward's street budget went into repaving, and new housing permits run sixth-highest. Then every measure of private money lands at the floor. More than a third of residents live below the poverty line, the worst rate of the fifty, and household income is second-lowest. On this scorecard the city's basic services are holding up here. The gap is in what residents earn.

Four of the ward's six worst rankings are modeled estimates of happiness, satisfaction and trust, built from demographics rather than from asking anyone who lives here. Those four are largely the poverty rate wearing different labels and should be read as one finding rather than four. This is also the quarter to write the baseline down. With the Obama Center opening nearby and the Woodlawn Central development approved, the poverty, income and permit lines on this page are the ones that will show whether any of that investment reaches the people already living here.
reading_the_rankings: The number to distrust most is the one that looks best. First place for socializing with neighbors weekly comes from the same demographic model that puts the ward last on happiness and 49th of 50 on trust, and its publisher rates it low confidence. A model that produces both extremes for one ward is describing its own inputs rather than the neighborhood. The street-resurfacing figure needs a different caution. It records how the ward office chose to spend its repair budget, a decision by an officeholder rather than a condition on the ground, and committing nearly all of a year's budget to one category says as much about the state of the streets as about anyone's priorities.

news.headline: Sprawling Woodlawn Central Development, Daily News Building Landmarking Get Zoning Approval
news.note: City Council's zoning committee approved the first phase of the $580 million Woodlawn Central mixed-use development, plus landmark status for the Chicago Daily News Building.

news.headline: South Side residents call for stronger housing protections as Obama Center's official opening nears
news.note: Community groups held a news conference in Woodlawn and nearby neighborhoods asking for rent control and other anti-displacement measures as the Obama Presidential Center opens.
